chunks: ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked him about the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, whether there is any takbir or tasbih in them.

He said: “No. They are only two sajdahs. If the one who forgot is the Imam, he says takbir when he performs sajdah and when he raises his head, so that those behind him may know that he has forgotten. There is no tasbih upon him in them, nor is there any tashahhud in them after the two sajdahs.”

key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations referred to in this ruling
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.تَسْبِيحٌ: formula of glorification recited in worship
key_terms.تَشَهُّدٌ: the testimony recited in the seated portion of salat
key_terms.تَكْبِيرٌ: saying 'Allahu Akbar' during the movement of the ritual act
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in salat

ai.seo_question: What is recited in the two prostrations of forgetfulness, and is there tashahhud after them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on Sajdat al-Sahw in salat. It states that they are simply two prostrations, with no tasbih and no tashahhud after them; however, if the one performing them is the Imam, he says takbir when going down and rising so the followers recognize his forgetfulness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.996 – Ammar al-Sabati asked him about the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdat al-Sahw), and whether there is any Takbir (saying "Allahu Akbar") or Tasbih (glorification) in them.

He (Imam Ja'far Al-Sadiq) replied: "No, they are simply two prostrations. If the one who forgot is the Imam, then he should say Takbir when he prostrates and when he raises his head, so that those behind him know that he has made a mistake. There is no need for him to say Tasbih in them, and there is no need for any Tashahhud (testification) after the two prostrations."
